column7: A complete key set assembled from two generations (for example one file restored from another backup) booted: presence was the only real check, and the same-group mtime heuristic could not see a set copied with cp/install/docker cp/kubectl cp, which stamp the current time; the server failed later at the first decrypt. Every key writer now records a SHA-256 per file in keyset.manifest.json (two-phase: staged before the first rename, committed after the last fsync), and boot refuses a file matching neither its recorded nor a staged hash, naming it. The heuristic and keySetMtimeTolerance are deleted. Also: TestEveryKeyMaterialWriterUpdatesTheManifest (structural guard over every writer in internal/encryption, internal/encryptionops, server/admin), TestRotateKEKCrashPoints_BootClassifiesAndRecovers (internal/encryption: the real rotate-kek crashed at all six checkpoints; boot finishes the hazard window from kek.salt.pending instead of failing with wrong passphrase), TestUpgrade_PreManifestInstallWithOldFallback_AdoptsThenSurvivesRotateKEK (warn-and-adopt on upgrade, old fallback blob not refused).
